1 Indoor Air Quality Station Maintenance Manual
This manual provides a structured framework for maintaining indoor air quality monitoring
stations across multiple sites. It covers routine procedures, calibration protocols, data validation,
and quality assurance to ensure reliable and accurate measurements. The guidance is designed
for facility managers, technicians, and environmental health officers responsible for station
upkeep and data integrity.
Supporting records are presented in Figure 1.
Routine Maintenance Procedures
Figure 1: Daily inspection tasks and responsible roles
Routine maintenance is essential for consistent station performance. This section outlines daily,
weekly, and monthly tasks, including sensor checks, filter replacements, and software updates.
Adherence to these schedules minimizes downtime and ensures data continuity.
1.1.1 Daily Inspection Checklist
Daily inspections involve verifying power status, checking for physical obstructions, and
confirming data transmission. Technicians should log any anomalies and escalate issues
according to the response timeline. A structured checklist helps maintain consistency across all
sites.

Sensor and Filter Checks
Sensors and filters require regular attention to prevent drift and contamination. This subsection
details visual inspection of sensor heads, replacement intervals for particulate filters, and

1.1.1.1.1 Particulate Sensor Cleaning
Particulate sensors accumulate dust, affecting accuracy. Cleaning with approved materials and
following manufacturer guidelines is necessary. Technicians should record cleaning dates and
observe post-cleaning readings to confirm sensor recovery.

Data Logging and Transmission
Reliable data logging and transmission are vital for continuous monitoring. This subsection
covers checking logger status, verifying network connectivity, and ensuring time
synchronization. Regular audits of data completeness help identify gaps early.

1.1.2 Weekly Performance Verification
Weekly verification includes comparing station readings with reference instruments and
reviewing calibration status. Discrepancies beyond acceptable limits trigger recalibration or
repair. Documentation of verification results supports quality assurance.

Documentation and Record Keeping
Accurate records of maintenance activities, calibration events, and data quality checks are
essential. This section describes logbook formats, digital record systems, and retention policies
to support audits and trend analysis.
2 Calibration and Quality Assurance
Calibration and quality assurance activities ensure measurement traceability and accuracy. This
part details calibration frequency, reference standards, and corrective actions for
out-of-tolerance results.
Calibration Protocols
Calibration protocols specify procedures for zero and span checks, use of certified reference
materials, and adjustment of sensor responses. Technicians must follow documented steps and
record all calibration data.
2.1.1 Calibration Frequency and Methods
Calibration frequency depends on sensor type and regulatory requirements. This subsection
outlines recommended intervals and methods, including multipoint calibration for critical sensors
and single-point checks for others.
Zero and Span Checks
Zero and span checks verify sensor baseline and response. Zero checks use clean air, while span
checks employ known concentrations. Results outside acceptance criteria require immediate
corrective action.
2.1.1.1.1 Reference Standards
Reference standards must be traceable and within validity. This subsection describes handling,
storage, and verification of standard gases and permeation tubes to maintain their integrity.

2.1.1.1.2 Calibration Records
Calibration records include dates, standards used, results, and technician signatures. These
records are retained for audit purposes and to track sensor performance over time.
Supporting records are presented in Table 5.
Corrective Actions for Drift
When drift is detected, technicians must investigate root causes, adjust or replace sensors, and
document actions. Follow-up checks ensure the issue is resolved and data quality is restored.
2.1.2 Data Validation and Reporting
Data validation involves screening for outliers, flagging invalid periods, and applying correction
factors. Validated data are compiled into reports for stakeholders, ensuring transparency and
reliability.
Audit and Review Procedures
Regular audits of maintenance and calibration records ensure compliance with protocols. Review
procedures include internal checks and periodic external assessments to identify areas for
improvement.
